_note: SEED — the ONLY hand-authored input to the component map. It carries the one thing a machine cannot derive from source: which SITUATION each composed component is the answer to (you cannot read 'a share of a bounded whole' out of arc-gauge.svelte). Everything else — the export name, the import path, the real prop list, and whether every shipped component is accounted for — is derived from source by generate-registry.mjs, which regenerates registry/component-map.{md,json} on every build (the outputs are gitignored like dist/ and shipped via package.json 'files'). The build FAILS if any shipped component is left out of this file, so a new component cannot ship unmapped: classify it under a situation, or name it a primitive, or the build is red. Props here are validated against the component's real $props(); a trailing '?' just marks a prop optional for the reader and is stripped before validation. A component that spreads ...rest onto another component of this package accepts that component's props too, and they validate the same way — FormButton is Button with the type fixed.

situations.title: A single labelled figure
situations.description: One headline metric that earns a tile — a figure with a label, an optional unit, and the state of the thing it measures.

components.name: StatCard
components.props: label, value, unit?, sub?, status?, valueTone?, icon?
components.insteadOf: a Card you hand-build with a label over a big number

situations.title: Several bare figures together
situations.description: A block of plain figures read at a glance — an 'at a glance' strip — where each number is too small to earn its own StatCard.

components.name: StatList
components.insteadOf: a hand-built <dl> or a stack of label/value <div>s

components.name: FactGrid
components.insteadOf: the same figures inside a Panel or DetailPanel that already supplies the card — StatList's own border would nest a box in a box; FactGrid is the borderless, wrapping-grid answer for that spot

situations.title: Comparing magnitudes across rows
situations.description: A small ranked set of labelled bars — a per-lane usage table, a token-burn chart — where a full StatCard per row would be too heavy.

components.name: BarRow
components.insteadOf: a <div> with an inline width:%% bar you style by hand

situations.title: A share of a bounded whole
situations.description: A part of a fixed total — a percentage, a capacity, a rate-limit window — read as one 0–100 figure.

components.name: ArcGauge
components.insteadOf: a hand-drawn SVG ring, or printing a bare "72%"

situations.title: A compact trend
situations.description: An inline time series in a row or card — a trend the eye reads at a glance, not a full Tier-1 chart.

components.name: Sparkline
components.insteadOf: a hand-built SVG polyline, or reaching for a charting library for a thumbnail

situations.title: The state of a thing
situations.description: The health or status of something. One state reads as a chip; several independent states read as a dot strip.

components.name: StatusBadge
components.insteadOf: a coloured <span> pill you tint by hand

components.name: Scorecard
components.insteadOf: a hand-built row of coloured dots for several on/off/warn checks

situations.title: The detail of one entity
situations.description: The surface for a single selected record — an eyebrow, a title, its status, and a close affordance over the body.

components.name: DetailPanel
components.props: title, eyebrow?, status?, statusLabel?, onClose?, children
components.insteadOf: a Card you hand-build with an eyebrow, a title row and a close button

situations.title: A catalogue of like things
situations.description: An index of many peer items — a responsive tile wall, or a sortable/filterable table of records.

components.name: TileGrid
components.insteadOf: a grid with fixed sm:grid-cols-* breakpoints you maintain per page

components.name: DataTableTanstack
components.insteadOf: a hand-built <table>, or the raw Table primitive wired to TanStack by hand

components.name: DataTableToolbar
components.insteadOf: a hand-built search + filter-chip bar above a table

situations.title: A titled section of a route
situations.description: The generic titled card every route reaches for — an optional header with icon, subtitle and actions over a body. The default answer to 'I need a card here'.

components.name: Panel
components.props: children, title?, subtitle?, description?, icon?, action?, footer?, tone?, pad?
components.insteadOf: raw Card + CardHeader + CardTitle assembled by hand on every route; also the settings section — there is no separate SettingsSection, `description` wraps, `footer` carries Save/Cancel, `tone="destructive"` is the danger zone

situations.title: A form the app itself describes
situations.description: A form whose fields the app writes out itself, validated by superforms and wired for accessibility by Formsnap. These wrappers put the label/description/error rhythm and the ARIA wiring in one place; the schema-described renderer above is for the other case, where the shape arrives at runtime.

components.name: FormField
components.insteadOf: a <div class="space-y-2"> you rebuild per field, per app

components.name: FormControl
components.insteadOf: wiring id/aria-describedby/aria-invalid onto the input by hand

components.name: FormLabel
components.insteadOf: a <Label> that does not turn destructive when its field errors

components.name: FormDescription
components.insteadOf: helper text the field's aria-describedby never points at

components.name: FormFieldErrors
components.insteadOf: hand-rendered {#each errors} blocks, styled differently in each app

components.name: FormFieldset
components.insteadOf: a bare <fieldset> with no error state

components.name: FormLegend
components.insteadOf: a <legend> styled per app

components.name: FormElementField
components.insteadOf: hand-indexing into an array field's errors

components.name: FormButton
components.insteadOf: remembering type="submit" on every form's Button — it forwards every Button prop and sets the type

situations.title: A form the server described
situations.description: A config object whose shape arrives at runtime as a JSON Schema plus a JSON Forms UI Schema — the renderer walks both and dispatches to this package's widgets. Anything it cannot dispatch renders flagged, never blank.

components.name: SchemaForm
components.props: schema, value, onChange, uischema?, disabled?, idPrefix?
components.insteadOf: a hand-written renderer over a home-grown hint vocabulary, which is how a field goes missing in silence

situations.title: Library data the app fetched
situations.description: The estate's shared document-library surfaces — a faceted catalogue, one collection's detail, one document's detail, a ranked search answer — rendered from plain props the app maps its own API responses into. The package never fetches and never routes: the app owns the query, the offset and every link. Configuration is the schema-driven half (SchemaForm); library data is fixed components because its shape is stable.

components.name: LibraryBrowse
components.props: documents, facets?, query?, total?, offset?, limit?, loading?, error?, onQueryChange?, onFacetChange?, onPageChange?, documentHref?, onOpenDocument?, toolbar?
components.insteadOf: a hand-built catalogue page: search box, facet rail, filter chips, results table and pager re-derived per app

components.name: CollectionDetail
components.props: collection, stats?, documents?, documentsTotal?, loading?, error?, documentsLoading?, documentsError?, onPageChange?, documentHref?, onOpenDocument?, actions?, children?
components.insteadOf: a bespoke collection page assembled from raw Card, a hand-built table and its own stat rows

components.name: DocumentDetail
components.props: document, loading?, error?, collectionHref?, onOpenCollection?, actions?, children?
components.insteadOf: a bespoke document page: identity dl, locations, tags and memberships hand-laid-out per app

components.name: SearchResults
components.props: results, query?, total?, loading?, error?, resultHref?, onOpen?, onRetry?
components.insteadOf: a hand-built ranked hit list minting its own highlight and relevance styling

situations.title: A document a machine read, with evidence outlined
situations.description: One page at a time, fitted to its pane both ways so an A4 statement and a tall receipt alike fill it, with what a reading points at outlined on the page — a hovered or clicked region with its label, a dashed 'where it looked' set, and a focus that zooms in and centres. The app supplies the page render (image, PDF canvas, anything) and the region coordinates as page fractions; this owns the fit/zoom/pan and the overlay only.

components.name: PageCanvas
components.props: pageCount, page, currentPage?, regions?, lookedRegions?, activeRegionId?, focusedRegionId?, zoom?
components.insteadOf: a hand-built page viewer per app (godswood's DocumentViewer, pebblestone's PdfViewer) each re-deriving fit/zoom/pan, now with no way to outline what was read (#839)

situations.title: The frame every route shares
situations.description: The standing chrome — the app shell and its nav, the one page-title treatment, the persistent right-hand context column, a foldable working list beside the page's own content.

components.name: AppShell
components.props: nav, currentPath, brandTitle?, actions?, context?, children
components.insteadOf: a bespoke nav rail + header layout per app

components.name: ShellControls
components.insteadOf: a scope row (entity, financial year, chart/table) hand-placed above the page body; the shell's top bar carries it

components.name: Segmented
components.insteadOf: a hand-built row of aria-pressed buttons for a small fixed choice

components.name: PageHeader
components.props: title?, eyebrow?, breadcrumbs?, icon?, subtitle?, info?, meta?, actions?
components.insteadOf: a hand-written <h1> and title bar (the drift gate fails this)

components.name: ContextColumn
components.insteadOf: a hand-built right-hand <aside> with a stat card and a detail pane

components.name: ListShell
components.insteadOf: a module hand-rolling its own foldable second column beside the rail — a queue, an inbox, a working list

components.name: AppIdentity
components.props: user, workspace?, role?, entitlements?, onSignOut, onAccountSettings?, onSwitchTheme?
components.insteadOf: a hand-rolled account/avatar dropdown wired to raw DropdownMenu.* + Avatar.*

situations.title: The settings destination
situations.description: The one settings surface: a grouped section list beside the section you are reading, inside AppShell’s content area (give AppShell padded={false}). Sections are grouped by whose setting it is — the person’s, then the workspace’s. The sections themselves are Panels.

components.name: SettingsShell
components.insteadOf: a hand-built two-pane settings layout, or a card of tab links in a grid, per app

situations.title: A dialog or overlay
situations.description: A modal task and the pieces around it — the dialog frame, a section within its body, a ⌘K palette, an inline (i) hint.

components.name: AppDialog
components.props: title, open, onOpenChange?, size?, children, footer?
components.insteadOf: raw Dialog.* parts assembled into a frame by hand

components.name: DialogSection
components.insteadOf: hand-drawn dividers and section labels inside a dialog body

components.name: CommandPalette
components.insteadOf: a bespoke ⌘K command menu wired to raw Command.*

components.name: InfoTip
components.insteadOf: a standing explainer banner, or a raw Tooltip you wire per use

situations.title: Empty, loading, or failed
situations.description: A surface with nothing to show yet, still loading, or that failed to load — the three non-happy states every data view needs.

components.name: EmptyState
components.insteadOf: a hand-centred 'Nothing here' message

components.name: LoadingState
components.insteadOf: a bare spinner or 'Loading…' you place by hand

components.name: ErrorState
components.insteadOf: a hand-built error message with a retry button

primitives._note: Standard shadcn-svelte / bits-ui primitives an agent already knows by name. Listed so the coverage gate can account for every shipped component, and so a consumer's drift gate could one day read this split from the shipped package instead of hardcoding it. Kept in lockstep with the PRIMITIVES set in the household check-ui-drift.mjs gate.
